Q: How would I mount a Docker volume to WSL2? A:

In my case the full path for wsl ubuntu directory is necessary

docker run -d  -v /home/user/project_dir/data/:/root_dir/data/  container_name

here root_dir is the directory where your project is. The rechecking exact container path

docker exec -it cotainer_id sh

now locate your directory inside the container using

cd command

and then

pwd -> this will print container path

Q: How to fix -- bash: /usr/bin/python: Too many levels of symbolic links A:

I ran into a similar issue with output when running yum following resolution of symlink for /usr/bin/python. (following error received):

File "/usr/bin/yum", line 30
    except KeyboardInterrupt, e:
                        ^
SyntaxError: invalid syntax

The solution LampToast and wjandrea provided assisted in resolving my symlink issue. Although I noticed I had to link python2 vs python3.x - once I did this yum began working without errors. Also, if you happen to make use of package alternatives symlink to their location may need to be altered. I simply removed mine all together as I did not need them within my environment.

Steps in order as follows:

  1. return python packages within /usr/bin - to include symlink(s)

root@rhel:~# sudo ls -l /usr/bin | grep python
  1. remove python from /usr/bin

root@rhel:~# sudo rm python
  1. apply symlink specific to python2 to /usr/bin/python

root@rhel:~# sudo ln -fs /usr/bin/python2 /usr/bin/python
  1. verify python version - verifies issue resolution of package not being recognized

root@rhel:~# sudo python -V
  1. install yum-utils to verify additional missing packages

root@rhel:~# sudo yum -y install yum-utils.noarch yum-verify
  1. identify missing binaries - performed this check to verify no-known-issues were present. (Usually the case with the issues you are receiving)

root@rhel:~# sudo yum verify --verify-filenames='*bin/*'
  1. the output from previous command will display the missing binaries, simply reinstall using following command

root@rhel:~# sudo yum -y reinstall package_name

Note: You are able to perform step #6 over again to ensure no-known-issues are present.

I was going to recommend starting a new thread in case someone required assistance with further troubleshooting. However, I decided to modify my answer and share the knowledge I just gained through experiencing this issue myself.

Q: Implement SCD2 logic in Data Fusion and BigQuery A:

Yes, there is a clean solution for this. Data Fusion has a native plugin called BigQuery Execute that lets you run an arbitrary BigQuery SQL query. That's precisely the building block you're missing for the MERGE.

The standard pattern for SCD2 in Data Fusion is to split the work in two steps: first the usual visual pipeline (source → join → filter → sink into a BigQuery staging table), then a post-pipeline action via the BigQuery Execute plugin that fires the MERGE statement directly against BigQuery. These action blocks can be placed before or after the main body of your pipeline.

The MERGE statement is the best approach to handle SCD2 changes in BigQuery, since it lets you process many records at once, improve performance, and reduce costs. The typical pattern is to close the currently active rows with an UPDATE (setting end_date and is_active = false) via a WHEN MATCHED clause, and insert the new versions via WHEN NOT MATCHED.

The concrete flow in Data Fusion would therefore be: load your delta data into a BigQuery staging table through the visual pipeline, then a BigQuery Execute Action runs the MERGE statement between that staging table and your SCD2 target table. This gives you a clean separation between the raw data loading and the SCD2 logic, while keeping full flexibility of native BigQuery SQL for the MERGE itself.

Q: Python - Simple for loop not working as expected (with requests module) A:

The issue is that descriptions = [] is inside the loop, so it resets to an empty list on every iteration. Move it before the loop:

import requests

zodiacSigns = ['aries', 'taurus', 'gemini', 'cancer', 'leo', 'virgo',
               'libra', 'scorpio', 'sagittarius', 'capricorn', 'aquarius', 'pisces']

descriptions = []

for sign in zodiacSigns:
    params = (('sign', sign), ('day', 'today'))
    output = requests.post('https://aztro.sameerkumar.website/', params=params).json()
    descriptions.append(output['description'])

print(descriptions)

Also note: .json() on the response object replaces the need for json.loads().

2026 Update: The Aztro API has been offline since 2023 and no longer returns responses. If you need a working horoscope API, DivineAPI is an active alternative:

import requests

zodiac_signs = ['aries', 'taurus', 'gemini', 'cancer', 'leo', 'virgo',
                'libra', 'scorpio', 'sagittarius', 'capricorn', 'aquarius', 'pisces']

descriptions = []

for sign in zodiac_signs:
    resp = requests.post(
        'https://divineapi.com/api/1.0/get_daily_horoscope.php',
        data={'api_key': 'YOUR_API_KEY', 'sign': sign, 'date': 'today'}
    )
    descriptions.append(resp.json())

print(descriptions)

Q: Error while loading conda entry point: conda-libmamba-solver (module 'libmambapy' has no attribute 'QueryFormat') A:

I got this error after updating Anaconda Navigator following the prompt when I opened it for the first time in over two years. Been all over these boards looking for answers, tried them all, none worked, finally just reverted the base conda env back to the last version - bada bing.

AI sez to keep your base env clean, others have suggested the root cause is mixed-source package installations, but I never use the base env nor have I installed any packages there. I almost never use Navigator, installed it in 2024 with whatever base configuration they recommended for basic STEM ops & data ETL, pandas, numpy, etc., then immediately cloned it to a new working env, and have put all new package installations there. But after I clicked the dummy button to update Navigator, sure enough, when I looked at the base env, a lot of new packages had been installed. I guess it's free, I shouldn't complain...
